_comment: MCP resource spec for #47 Mission/Vision/Strategy Alignment Checker. Phase 2 .mcpb bundle target. Draft 2026-05-17.

resource.name: Mission / Vision / Strategy Alignment Checker
resource.description: Paste mission, vision, and current quarter's strategy doc. Surfaces drift between the three, platitudes, operational gaps in named bets, and a Rumelt diagnosis of the strategy.

tools.name: alignment_drift_map
tools.description: LLM-narrated. Three pairwise comparisons (mission-vs-vision, mission-vs-strategy, vision-vs-strategy) with drift severity and a 10-word drift label per pair.

tools.name: alignment_platitude_detector
tools.description: LLM-narrated. Lists empty phrases in each doc, verbatim, with what each would have to say to be load-bearing.

tools.name: alignment_operational_gaps
tools.description: LLM-narrated. Extracts named bets from the strategy and produces the questions the user should ask team leads to test operational follow-through. In Phase 1, output is questions. In Phase 2 with roadmap files, output is assertions.

team_roadmaps._phase_note: Phase 1 omits this array; Phase 2 .mcpb populates it from local roadmap files.

tools.name: alignment_rumelt_diagnosis
tools.description: LLM-narrated. Direct application of Rumelt's diagnosis test to the strategy doc only.

tools.name: alignment_quarterly_diff
tools.description: MCP-only (stateful). Compares this quarter's mission/vision/strategy against last quarter's. Surfaces drift direction (did the strategy drift away from the mission, or did the mission drift to follow the strategy?).
tools._phase_note: Web version does not expose this. Quarterly diff requires persisted prior triples, which is .mcpb scope.

tools.name: alignment_board_prep
tools.description: MCP-only. Outputs a one-page board pre-read artifact summarizing the drift map, Rumelt verdict, and the three highest-leverage operational gaps.

_open_questions: Validate ui:// URI scheme against current MCP Apps spec.
Drift-map visualization: in Phase 1 web, render the three-box arrow diagram as inline SVG or as CSS-grid blocks? Inline SVG scales; CSS-grid is lighter.
Platitude detector: should the list of flagged phrase patterns be user-editable (a team's actual platitudes vary), or locked? Locked is simpler but misses team-specific jargon.
Board-prep tool: should the output Markdown, PDF, or a structured JSON the user converts? PDF requires a Worker dependency; Markdown is most flexible.
_proposed_answers: Confirmed valid. The Jan 2026 MCP Apps spec uses ui:// for embedded UI resources. 'ui://working-from-lenny/alignment' matches the required pattern.

Inline SVG for the drift-map visualization. The three-box diagram has semantic content (drift direction, severity) that CSS-grid cannot encode without custom classes. Inline SVG scales to card width, allows color-coding arrows by severity (none/low/med/high with a four-color scale), and renders without an external dependency. Note: this answers the HTML build question gated on owner sign-off per PROCEDURAL_REFERENCE.md; no code change made here.

Lock the base pattern list; add a custom_phrases optional array to the inputSchema for team-specific overrides. This gives teams a lightweight escape hatch per-run without opening the base list to per-user configuration that would complicate corpus maintenance. A custom_phrases: string[] input field costs nothing to add now and does not require schema versioning.

Markdown output for Phase 2. PDF would require a headless rendering dependency (Puppeteer or a Worker with wasm) that is out of scope for the Jan 2026 .mcpb bundle format. Structured JSON shifts formatting burden to the user. Markdown is immediately usable in Notion, Linear, or a Google Doc paste, which is where board pre-reads actually live. Use a fixed Markdown template with three named sections matching the tool's output fields. Phase 3 can add PDF once the rendering story is clearer.
